name: Sun Tzu, Today — Mon/Wed/Fri episode (front-end for the YakYak engine)

nodes.name: Mon Wed Fri
nodes.notes: 06:00 UTC Mon/Wed/Fri — CADENCE=mwf in show/SunTzuToday/show.env. Use 'Test workflow' to fire a run by hand (note: manual runs don't advance the maxim cursor).

nodes.name: Show config
nodes.notes: ALL per-show config lives here, on the canvas — the workflow reads no environment variables. Required: campaignId (a campaign the API credential's account owns) and userId (for the balance check). Optional: soundtrackAudioPath (empty = skip the pin), chatWebhookUrl (empty = no announcement). corpusUrl defaults to the cookbook corpus on GitHub — point it at your fork to edit the corpus.

nodes.name: Fetch user
nodes.notes: Same 'YakYak API' Bearer credential as the engine — no token on the canvas or in env. onError=continue so Balance guard can report a clear error instead of a bare 404.

nodes.name: Fetch corpus
nodes.notes: The public-domain corpus (Art of War, Lionel Giles 1910, Project Gutenberg #132) fetched from the cookbook repo — the showrunner reads the same file from its checkout. No corpus = no episode, so this node fails hard.

nodes.name: Pick maxim
nodes.notes: The Extracted archetype's cursor: one maxim per episode, walked sequentially, looping when the corpus is exhausted.

parameters.jsCode:
const TPL = "You are the head writer for "Sun Tzu, Today", a short-form video series that
takes ONE verbatim maxim from Sun Tzu's Art of War and stages it as a self-contained
modern micro-drama. Real, timeless strategy applied to a relatable contemporary dilemma.

TODAY'S MAXIM (quote it VERBATIM — do not paraphrase):
  "{{MAXIM}}"
  — {{VERSEREF}}, The Art of War (Sun Tzu, tr. Lionel Giles, 1910; public domain)

CAST (only these three may speak; each scene's leading character must be one of them):
  - The Strategist — a timeless Sun Tzu-style mentor. MUST be the leading character in
    Scene 1 (states today's maxim as a cold open) and Scene 7 (closes by re-stating the
    maxim as the takeaway). Calm, grave, economical with words.
  - The Student — a modern young professional facing one concrete, relatable dilemma
    (a toxic boss, a bidding war, a betrayal, a negotiation, a breakup, a startup gamble).
  - The Rival — the adversary in that dilemma (boss / competitor / opponent). Sharp, cold.

TONE: Cinematic, a little noir, quietly intense. The drama is ordinary modern life;
the gravity comes from the ancient maxim landing on it. No violence-glorifying, no slurs.

STRUCTURE — exactly 7 scenes:
  1. The Strategist states today's maxim (verbatim) as a cold open.
  2–3. The Student's modern dilemma; The Rival escalates it.
  4–5. The Student applies the maxim and turns the situation.
  6. The resolution.
  7. The Strategist closes, re-stating the maxim verbatim — this is the screenshot caption card.

PER-SCENE REQUIREMENTS:
  - ~200 words of prose describing visuals, action and atmosphere (brief it like a
    director: location, light, what just happened, what's happening now). Lean on the
    chiaroscuro ink-and-steel look: deep shadow, one warm gold light.
  - Exactly ONE spoken dialog line per scene, 8–12 words, attributed to the leading
    character. Make it land. Do NOT end the dialog line with a period ("!" or "?" are fine).
  - Only the three cast may speak.

OUTPUT — reply with ONLY the markdown document below — no preamble, no
triple-backtick fences, nothing after it:

  # Sun Tzu, Today — {{VERSEREF}}
  **Generated (UTC):** {{TS}}
  **Maxim:** "{{MAXIM}}" — {{VERSEREF}}, The Art of War (tr. Lionel Giles, 1910)

  ## Social title: <punchy title for social posting, 50 characters MAX>

  ## Headlines we drew from:
  - "{{MAXIM}}" — {{VERSEREF}}, The Art of War (Sun Tzu)

  ## Scene 1 — <short title>
  **Leading character:** The Strategist
  **Dialog:** "<8–12 word line>"

  <~200 words of scene prose>

  ... (continue through Scene 7, which is again The Strategist) ...";

// The Sun Tzu, Today head-writer prompt, adapted from show/SunTzuToday/compute.js.
// One change vs the showrunner original: the file-write OUTPUT step becomes
// "reply with only the markdown", plus a requested '## Social title:' line so
// ONE model call covers both the story and the ≤50-char social title.
const ts = new Date().toISOString();
const p = $json;
const fill = (t, map) => t.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (m, k) => (map[k] === undefined ? m : map[k]));
const prompt = fill(TPL, { TS: ts, MAXIM: p.maxim, VERSEREF: p.verseRef });
return [{ json: { prompt } }];

nodes.name: Write story (Claude)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { model: 'claude-opus-4-8', max_tokens: 16000, thinking: { type: 'adaptive' }, messages: [ { role: 'user', content: $json.prompt } ] } }}

nodes.notes: Messages API over raw HTTP (no SDK inside n8n). Auth via the 'Anthropic API key' Header Auth credential (header name x-api-key). Adaptive thinking; the story lands in the response's text block.

nodes.name: Build story payload
nodes.notes: The story markdown is preserved on this node's output — n8n's execution log is the story archive (the showrunner's stories/ equivalent).

nodes.name: Call engine

workflowId.cachedResultName: YakYak engine — resolve target, patch or new episode, render, post

nodes.notes: Fires the generic YakYak engine in episode mode. The engine only responds once the episode is generated AND rendered. Retry is safe: a re-run lands on the same unrendered slot. Announcement happens here (below), not in the engine.

nodes.name: Set social fields

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ Object.assign({ movieId: $json.movieId }, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle ? { socialTitle: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle } : {}, $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption ? { socialDescription: $('Build story payload').first().json.socialCaption } : {}) }}

nodes.notes: Showrunner parity: ≤50-char social title + caption. onError=continue — cosmetic metadata must not kill a rendered episode.

nodes.name: Announce

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { text: '⚔️ Sun Tzu, Today episode ready — "' + ($('Build story payload').first().json.socialTitle || 'Latest maxim') + '": ' + $('Call engine').first().json.url } }}

nodes.notes: Review-first output event (the safe default). chatWebhookUrl empty → this node errors and the run still succeeds (onError=continue). Auto-posting to social is the deliberate next step — see the BBN guide §4.3.
